title: Perfect Security
statementMd:
Alice has a very important message $*M*$ consisting of some non-negative integers that she wants to keep secret from Eve. Alice knows that the only theoretically secure cipher is one-time pad. Alice generates a random key $*K*$ of the length equal to the message's length. Alice computes the bitwise xor of each element of the message and the key (![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/0c01d57961927bc12eb51d8197470990daaaa8de.png), where ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c4b7092c0f7ce6535f2574569c98f7b3c2fe2c5f.png) denotes the [bitwise XOR operation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitwise_operation#XOR)) and stores this encrypted message $*A*$. Alice is smart. Be like Alice.

For example, Alice may have wanted to store a message $*M* = (0, 15, 9, 18)$. She generated a key $*K* = (16, 7, 6, 3)$. The encrypted message is thus $*A* = (16, 8, 15, 17)$.

Alice realised that she cannot store the key with the encrypted message. Alice sent her key $*K*$ to Bob and deleted her own copy. Alice is smart. Really, be like Alice.

Bob realised that the encrypted message is only secure as long as the key is secret. Bob thus randomly permuted the key before storing it. Bob thinks that this way, even if Eve gets both the encrypted message and the key, she will not be able to read the message. Bob is not smart. Don't be like Bob.

In the above example, Bob may have, for instance, selected a permutation $(3, 4, 1, 2)$ and stored the permuted key $*P* = (6, 3, 16, 7)$.

One year has passed and Alice wants to decrypt her message. Only now Bob has realised that this is impossible. As he has permuted the key randomly, the message is lost forever. Did we mention that Bob isn't smart?

Bob wants to salvage at least some information from the message. Since he is not so smart, he asks for your help. You know the encrypted message $*A*$ and the permuted key $*P*$. What is the lexicographically smallest message that could have resulted in the given encrypted text?

More precisely, for given $*A*$ and $*P*$, find the lexicographically smallest message $*O*$, for which there exists a permutation $π$ such that ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a13e05dbed3e9a47b9d8d6d0f07297a940549234.png) for every $*i*$.

Note that the sequence $*S*$ is lexicographically smaller than the sequence $*T*$, if there is an index $*i*$ such that $*S*_{*i*} < *T*_{*i*}$ and for all $*j* < *i*$ the condition $*S*_{*j*} = *T*_{*j*}$ holds.

## Input

The first line contains a single integer $*N*$ ($1 ≤ *N* ≤ 300000$), the length of the message.

The second line contains $*N*$ integers $*A*_{1}, *A*_{2}, ..., *A*_{*N*}$ ($0 ≤ *A*_{*i*} < 2^{30}$) representing the encrypted message.

The third line contains $*N*$ integers $*P*_{1}, *P*_{2}, ..., *P*_{*N*}$ ($0 ≤ *P*_{*i*} < 2^{30}$) representing the permuted encryption key.

## Output

Output a single line with $*N*$ integers, the lexicographically smallest possible message $*O*$. Note that all its elements should be non-negative.

## Note

In the first case, the solution is $(10, 3, 28)$, since ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a896b30a69636d1bfbfa981eae10650f5fee843c.png), ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e383e4333ea37c4652ce2ac1ccfc2cfcf96e0896.png) and ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c24ed3c6f88805eb3710487b3fe07ff64034151a.png). Other possible permutations of key yield messages $(25, 6, 10)$, $(25, 3, 15)$, $(10, 21, 10)$, $(15, 21, 15)$ and $(15, 6, 28)$, which are all lexicographically larger than the solution.
statementZhMd:
Alice 有一条由若干个非负整数组成的重要消息 $*M*$，她希望对 Eve 保密。Alice 知道，从理论上来说唯一安全的密码是一次一密。Alice 生成了一个长度与消息长度相等的随机密钥 $*K*$。Alice 将消息中的每个元素与密钥中对应的元素进行按位异或（![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/0c01d57961927bc12eb51d8197470990daaaa8de.png)，其中 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c4b7092c0f7ce6535f2574569c98f7b3c2fe2c5f.png) 表示[按位异或运算](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitwise_operation#XOR)），并将加密后的消息 $*A*$ 保存下来。Alice 很聪明。向 Alice 学习。

例如，Alice 可能想要保存消息 $*M*$ = (0, 15, 9, 18)。她生成了密钥 $*K*$ = (16, 7, 6, 3)。因此，加密后的消息为 $*A*$ = (16, 8, 15, 17)。

Alice 意识到她不能将密钥与加密后的消息保存在一起。Alice 将密钥 $*K*$ 发送给 Bob，然后删除了自己的副本。Alice 很聪明。真的，要向 Alice 学习。

Bob 意识到，只有在密钥保密的情况下，加密后的消息才是安全的。因此，Bob 在保存密钥之前将其随机打乱。Bob 认为这样一来，即使 Eve 同时得到了加密后的消息和密钥，她也无法读懂消息。Bob 不聪明。不要向 Bob 学习。

在上面的例子中，Bob 可能选择了一个排列 $(3, 4, 1, 2)$，并保存打乱后的密钥 $*P*$ = (6, 3, 16, 7)。

一年过去了，Alice 想要解密她的消息。直到这时 Bob 才意识到这是不可能的。由于他随机打乱了密钥，消息永远丢失了。我们提过 Bob 不聪明吗？

Bob 想至少挽救消息中的一部分信息。由于他不太聪明，于是向你寻求帮助。你知道加密后的消息 $*A*$ 和打乱后的密钥 $*P*$。在所有可能由给定加密文本得到的消息中，字典序最小的消息是什么？

更准确地说，对于给定的 $*A*$ 和 $*P*$，请找出字典序最小的消息 $*O*$，使得存在一个排列 $π$，对于每个 $*i*$ 都满足 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a13e05dbed3e9a47b9d8d6d0f07297a940549234.png)。

注意，如果存在一个下标 $*i*$，使得 $*S*_{*i*} < *T*_{*i*}$，并且对于所有 $*j* < *i*$ 都有 $*S*_{*j*} = *T*_{*j*}$，则称序列 $*S*$ 的字典序小于序列 $*T*$。

## 输入格式

第一行包含一个整数 $*N*$（$1 ≤ *N* ≤ 300000$），表示消息的长度。

第二行包含 $*N*$ 个整数 $*A*_{1}, *A*_{2}, ..., *A*_{*N*}$（$0 ≤ *A*_{*i*} < 2^{30}$），表示加密后的消息。

第三行包含 $*N*$ 个整数 $*P*_{1}, *P*_{2}, ..., *P*_{*N*}$（$0 ≤ *P*_{*i*} < 2^{30}$），表示打乱后的加密密钥。

## 输出格式

输出一行包含 $*N*$ 个整数，即字典序最小的可能消息 $*O*$。注意，其所有元素都应为非负数。

## 说明

在第一种情况下，答案为 $(10, 3, 28)$，因为 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a896b30a69636d1bfbfa981eae10650f5fee843c.png)、![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e383e4333ea37c4652ce2ac1ccfc2cfcf96e0896.png) 和 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c24ed3c6f88805eb3710487b3fe07ff64034151a.png)。密钥的其他可能排列会得到消息 $(25, 6, 10)$、$(25, 3, 15)$、$(10, 21, 10)$、$(15, 21, 15)$ 和 $(15, 6, 28)$，它们的字典序都大于答案。
